newsitem.title: USA: R.R. Donnelley net hurt by lower directory revenue.
newsitem.headline: R.R. Donnelley net hurt by lower directory revenue.

text.p: R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co. said Thursday its earnings fell 30 percent for the second quarter, hurt by lower revenues from its directory printing business.

Donnelley, the leading U.S. printing company, reported net income of $37.7 million, or 26 cents a share, in the second quarter, compared with net income of $54.3 million, or 35 cents a share, a year earlier.
The results were in line with analysts' expectations, according to market research firm First Call.
Net sales declined $64 million, or 4 percent for the second quarter, to $1.504 billion.
Donnelley said revenue gains in most business units, including book and financial printing, were more than offset by lower directory printing revenues.
The company's reduced stakes in Metromail Corp. and Donnelley Enterprise Solutions Inc., which had initial public offerings in 1996, also reduced revenues.

"Although development, start-up and restructuring-related expenses affected our results for the first six months, our continued concentration on and investment in our core printing business should produce an improved earnings trend in the second half of the year," Chief Executive Officer William Davis said.
The company also announced a 5.3 percent increase in the quarterly dividend, to 20 cents a share from 19 cents a share.
R.R. Donnelley's stock declined 6 cents to $40 a share in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
